protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED recording of gate-harness-naming.v3 plus operative rider RB-GHN-V3-A1
summary: Subject and prompt held. Every attack on the arithmetic fails, and fails by construction rather than by assertion: D-002's required set expands to nineteen, minus G17 it is order-equal to v3's eighteen, and eighteen minus the two D-006-blocked gates is exactly sixteen. The entry states the honest projection as 16 of 18 and explicitly refuses 16 of 16. One defect survives, and it is in the operative rider. RB-GHN-V3-A1 ends with the bare instruction 'Remove the word "countable"' with no target named. The replacement text it supplies already contains no such word, so under the narrow reading the instruction does nothing. Under the broad reading it reaches the only two occurrences left in v3, and both of them are refusals that quote the term in order to forbid it — the very guardrails erected against GHN-V2-B1, which this same entry cites as its reason for rejecting 16 of 16.

objections.location: Subject, section 'Operative rider RB-GHN-V3-A1', final paragraph: 'Remove the word "countable". Do not present 16 as the required-gate denominator.'
objections.claim: The removal instruction names no target. Scoped to the replaced sentence it is inert; read as a further instruction it deletes two protective refusals and disarms the artifact's defence against the exact error the next sentence prohibits.
objections.why: v3 contains exactly three occurrences of the string 'countable', which I located by offset rather than by reading for them. One is item 7 of remainingUnmetNamed, 'MF-6 file-08 write of *countable* identifiers into the Platform matrix / harness column', and that is the sentence the rider replaces. The replacement text the rider supplies contains no 'countable', so for that sentence the removal is already accomplished and restating it adds nothing. The other two occurrences are the ones the instruction can still reach, and neither is a use of the term — both are refusals that name it in scare quotes in order to forbid the concept. authorityClaim reads 'Does not invent a smaller \'countable required\' required-set.' whatThisDoesNotDo reads 'Does not replace D-001/D-002's required-gate set with a \'countable required\' set.' Remove the word from those and they degrade to 'a smaller \'required\' required-set' and 'a \'required\' set' — the sentences survive as grammar and stop functioning as refusals. Those two refusals are not incidental. They are the guardrails v3 added in response to GHN-V2-B1, the blocker recorded in v3's own predecessorVerdictFindings as 'requiredNow restored to 18 … G03/G04 remain in the required denominator', and this entry cites that same finding at 'Present 16 of 16. Rejected: GHN-V2-B1.' So the broad reading of the rider would strip the artifact's stated defence against precisely the error the rider's own next sentence forbids. The neighbouring sentence shows the distinction that is missing: 'Do not present 16 as the required-gate denominator' is a conduct constraint on the future write, and it already appears in v3 twice. 'Remove the word' is an edit instruction, and an edit instruction needs a target.
objections.whyNotMustFix: The narrow reading is genuinely available — the sentence sits immediately after the replacement block and can be read as describing that block's purpose — so this is an ambiguity that invites the destructive act rather than one that commits it. The rider is operative and binds a later MF-6 write and a v3 successor, which is why an unscoped edit instruction should not be adopted as written.
objections.repair: Scope the removal. For example: 'Remove the word "countable" from that sentence only. The refusals in authorityClaim and whatThisDoesNotDo name "countable required" in order to forbid it and are retained verbatim.'

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, decision clause 3: 'Condition 4 stays PARTLY MET. Owners remain 22 of 22. Named-harness half remains 0 of 18 in file 08'
notesNonBlocking.observation: The two halves of condition 4 are reported in adjacent sentences against different denominators, 22 and 18. Both figures are independently true and correctly attributed — I confirmed all 22 gate rows in file 08 carry an Owner value, and that the required-now set is 18 — and the difference is principled, since owner naming covers every gate row while harness naming is measured against the required set. It is recorded only because a later reader meeting '22 of 22' and '0 of 18' in consecutive sentences could take the first as a statement about condition 4 as a whole. Naming the denominators, as clause 3 already does for the harness half, would remove the risk entirely.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 49732971b7ccd3cc596f7b1da3aee82a5a1f7f1a35394988d31000958b06844d, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 394ec9c3… across start and end.

The attack 'presents 16 of 16 as the required denominator' fails, and the arithmetic is right by construction rather than by assertion. I expanded D-002's condition-4 required-gate set from COORD myself, unwrapping the blockquote prefix and the G01..G05 range, and it yields exactly nineteen. Removing G17 leaves eighteen, and that list is not merely set-equal but order-equal to the eighteen gates v3 marks REQUIRED or REQUIRED-SCOPED. Subtracting the recordable subset from the required set returns exactly {DR-G03, DR-G04}, so 'presently recordable required names are 16' and '16 of 18, not 16 of 16' are both derivable from v3's own gate records without taking any of v3's summary fields on trust.

The attack 'counts G03/G04 as named' fails on the artifact's own classification and on the entry's text. Both carry sliceStanding REQUIRED-BUT-NAMING-BLOCKED-ON-D006-MACHINE-PINS and namingStanding IDENTIFIER-RESERVED-ZERO-C4-PROGRESS, they remain inside the required eighteen, and clause 2 says 'G03/G04 remain required and unnamed until a D-006-conforming successor.' The header adds 'Does not pin G03/G04 machines.'

The attack 'restores G17 as required-now' fails on four surfaces: the header's 'Does not restore SARIF or G17', clause 2's 'G17 is dropped (D-077)', the alternative 'Restore G17. Rejected: D-077', and v3's own sliceStanding INAPPLICABLE-DROPPED-BY-D077 with namingStanding HISTORICAL-IDENTIFIER-RETAINED-NOT-COUNTED. G17 is absent from the eighteen.

The attack 'this entry itself writes file 08 or claims condition 4 MET' fails. The header, clause 4 and the readiness effect each refuse the file-08 write; clause 3 keeps condition 4 PARTLY MET and clause 2's projection ends 'and still not MET'. file 08 measures ff2ebadd…, matching the citation, and git reports it unmodified in my working tree. I also checked the substance rather than the label: the file-08 gate table contains zero occurrences of the harness.DR-G identifier form, so 'Named-harness half remains 0 of 18 in file 08' is true of the bytes and not only of the entry's account of them.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED / QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED' fails on a line-by-line audit rather than a keyword count. Every occurrence in the subject is a refusal or a standing statement: three SATISFIED all negated, QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED both inside 'Does not claim', and the four MET occurrences are 'Does not make condition 4 MET', 'stays PARTLY MET' twice and 'still not MET'. No status token is coined or elevated.

The attack 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fails: both occurrences are refusals, at the header and at clause 4, the alternative 'Authorize implementation. Rejected: condition 5 remains last' is present, and the directory does not exist.

The attack 'GHN-V3-A1 ignored (no rider)' fails — a rider exists, is named operative in clause 1, and carries substantive replacement text. Its effect on v3 is an improvement on the sentence it targets: 'countable identifiers' is undefined and is the loaded term, while 'presently recordable required identifiers' is the category v3 defines, and both prohibitions in the original are retained. My objection concerns the removal instruction that follows, not the replacement itself.

I tested the replacement's shortening of 'the Platform matrix / harness column' to 'the harness column' as a possible loss of scope and cleared it. file 08 has exactly one column whose header is 'Platform matrix / harness', so the shortened form names the same single column unambiguously and no second write target is dropped.

The two rejection grounds are accurate, which I checked against the findings' own recorded text rather than their labels. GHN-V1-B2's repair reads 'G03/G04 reclassified IDENTIFIER-RESERVED-ZERO-C4-PROGRESS; they do not count toward condition 4 naming', which is what 'Count G03/G04 as named. Rejected: GHN-V1-B2' relies on. GHN-V2-B1's reads 'requiredNow restored to 18 … Projected effect is 16 of 18. G03/G04 remain in the required denominator', which is what 'Present 16 of 16. Rejected: GHN-V2-B1' relies on.

The entry's account of my own verdict is exact. gate-harness-naming.v3.review-independent.claude2.json is mine, hashes to ba7f48c3… as cited, and records verdict ACCEPT with blockers 0 and advisories 0.

Five of the six measured inputs match live bytes: file 08 ff2ebadd…, v3 b5236612…, my v3 verdict ba7f48c3…, the Codex v3 verdict b5162d99… hashed without opening, and the D-056 commit 75c981dd…, which resolves to 'D-056: SATISFIED-vs-qualification successor amendment'. The sixth is addressed below.

The COORD pin e6575389… no longer matches live bytes, which now measure 236a97fa…, and I traced the cause rather than reporting the mismatch bare. COORD moved because D-087 was adopted and committed at 953b23116e337ca289a2a02613753697119cfbf9 after D-086's dispatch measurement; e6575389… is exactly COORD as of the D-056 commit. The entry's table is labelled 'Measured inputs at dispatch' and carries the clause 'If a cited file moves, re-measure', so this is anticipated movement rather than a false pin, and I raise it as neither MUST-FIX nor SHOULD-FIX. Nothing in the entry depends on the deleted D-056 recital: 'D-056 is ADOPTED at 75c981dd' and 'This entry does not overturn D-056' both remain true after D-087. The COORD pin should be re-measured to 236a97fa… at adoption, which is what the entry's own clause directs.

The form citation holds. D-035 and D-042 are both present in COORD as 'Record doctor-contract.v4 as DR-114's accepted design contract' and 'Record permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate', the same record-an-accepted-candidate shape as D-086. D-077 is present and is the entry that drops G17. D-086 is absent from COORD, so adoption creates no collision.

v3's own posture is still that of a candidate and this entry does not disturb it: status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL. The reversibility clause matches the act in both limbs, total before any dependent MF-6 write and requiring restoration of harness cells after one lands.

G13 and G06/G11 are characterised correctly and are outside the eighteen. G13 carries BLOCKED-ON-DR-118 with IDENTIFIER-RESERVED-ZERO-C4-PROGRESS, matching 'a zero-progress reservation pending DR-118'; G06 and G11 carry HYGIENE-ONLY-NOT-SLICE-1-REQUIRED, matching D-002's 'G06/G11: NOT slice-1-required'.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The entry's numbers are the strongest part of it — I rebuilt every one of them from D-002 and from v3's gate records without relying on a summary field, and they close exactly, including the order-equality of D-002-minus-G17 with v3's eighteen. The defect is not in the recording but in the rider attached to it. An operative rider is an instruction that will be executed later by someone reading it without this context, and 'Remove the word "countable"' with no target, placed after a replacement that has already removed the only use of the word, points at two refusals that exist to forbid the concept the word names. That those refusals are the specific repair for GHN-V2-B1 — the finding this entry cites two sections later as its reason to reject 16 of 16 — is what moves this from pedantry to a real risk. One scoping clause fixes it.
